attributes.residual: MECHANISM, NAMED AND COMPLETE, from the aligned view (`fnasm game/ui/btext FontHeight --diff`). 22/22 instructions, opcode multiset IDENTICAL, and the ONLY difference is WHERE three epilogue restores sit. Target hoists them into the float-latency shadow: `lwz r0,44(r1)` at +0x2c (immediately after r0's last use at the `stw r0,24(r1)` of the int-to-float magic pair), `mtlr r0` at +0x34 (between `lfd f0,24(r1)` and `fsubs`), and `lfd f31,32(r1)` at +0x40 (immediately after f31's last reader, the `fmuls f0,f0,f31` at +0x3c). Ours emits all three as an unscheduled block at the bottom: `lwz r0,44(r1)` +0x44, `lfd f31,32(r1)` +0x48, `addi r1,r1,40` +0x4c, `mtlr r0` +0x50. WHY IT IS NOT A SPELLING PROBLEM: the same three-source-form matrix left the five clusters bit-for-bit unmoved in (a) and (c), and (b) moved only the frame. WHY OUR SCHEDULER STOPS: the one atom that must cross a STORE to reach its target slot is `lfd f31,32(r1)`, which in the target is issued ABOVE `stfd f0,16(r1)`; ours never moves a stack load above a stack store to a different slot, and the same function's sibling TextHeightMLines DOES hoist `lfd f31,64(r1)` where no store intervenes -- so the blocker is store/load stack disambiguation, not an inability to hoist. POSTPROCESSOR CANDIDACY (for the WebFrank lane, source-exhaustion trail = THIS record): the three atoms are pairwise independent -- `lwz r0,44(r1)` writes g0 and reads stack(44); `mtlr r0` reads g0 and writes LR; `lfd f31,32(r1)` writes f31 and reads stack(32) -- the window contains exactly one store (`stfd f0,16(r1)`, slot 16, disjoint from 32 and 44), no control instruction and no relocation, and `addi r1,r1,40` is AFTER both stack reads in both streams so r1 is never redefined under them. This is the same mechanism CLASS as this TU's existing DrawGlowTextMLines pin (epilogue restore permutation, stages copy_register_fields + instruction_permutation). It is NOT proven: the window is wider than DrawGlowTextMLines' and crosses a store, so check_permutation_dependences must be RUN, not assumed.
